Hi Sara — great to see the RFP. Short answers up front, then a proposed baseline we can land on: 

1) Billing model: embeddings are billed per-vector for hosted API. We convert to per-1k-vector blocks for invoicing (so 1,000 vectors billed as 1 unit). Generative endpoints remain per-token.

2) Supported models / dims (hosted):
   - rw-embed-compact-v1 — 768 dims (low-cost, good for classification / small-scale nearest-neighbor)
   - rw-embed-std-v2 — 1536 dims (default: best balance for semantics + retrieval)
   - rw-embed-large-v1 — 3072 dims (higher fidelity for dense retrieval / fine-grained similarity)
   - rw-embed-quant-4096-q4 — 4096 dims (quantized variant for high-accuracy searching with reduced memory footprint)

3) Committed discounts: we typically publish a standard rate card (attached) and offer commit discounts by tier. Below are illustrative baseline public-ish numbers (we can provide a formal quote):
   - On-demand (no commit): $0.00055 per vector (1536-d default)
   - 10M/mo commit: 12% discount off on-demand
   - 25M/mo commit: 22% discount off on-demand
   - 100M+ / enterprise reserved: 35%+ (includes options for Dedicated capacity pricing)

4) Latency & batching guidance: for hosted API, expected p50 for single-call 1536-d embeddings is ~35-60ms; p95 around 180-350ms depending on load and region. For batch requests (up to 1k vectors per request) you should expect better throughput; we recommend continuous batching to amortize GPU kernel costs. We'll include SE notes in next message.

Attached: Redwood_Embeddings_Ratecard_v1.pdf (pdf) — this is a baseline; final pricing requires volume, term, and PO details. Also attaching a one-page SOC2/network snapshot for procurement.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week to go line-by-line. If you can share your preferred commit level (10M / 25M / 100M) and desired term (6/12/24 months), we can produce a formal quote and draft SOW.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Embeddings rate card + dims question (Nimble RFP)

Sean / Monica — some quick SE notes you can paste into the formal reply: 

- Dimension trade-offs: 1536-d (rw-embed-std-v2) is good default; it gives solid recall and smaller index size. 3072-d is ~2x compute and memory but can improve nearest-neighbor quality for very high-similarity tasks. 4096-q4 is a quantized option we recommend only if Nimble wants best-in-class recall and is comfortable with approximate vectors in exchange for lower serving memory.
- Batch sizing: our hosted endpoint supports batch sizes up to 2,048 vectors per call, but practical sweet spot is 256-1024 for best latency/throughput tradeoff. For 40M/month we recommend ingest pipelines that push 1k batches during off-peak ingestion windows.
- Throughput: With continuous batching you can expect ~120k-300k vectors/sec per dedicated GPU pool (depends on model and quantization). Hosted API throughput and p95 are conservative — if Nimble needs hard p95 SLAs at peak, we should discuss Dedicated capacity.
- Caching: If there are repeated embedding requests (deduped user docs), enable our prefix KV cache — can reduce vector counts billed.

Feel free to ping me to join the call if they want a deeper dive on indexing and memory sizing.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
